hypothesis: GDSC — Geodetic Dilatational Strain Corridor: blind transtensional relay/jog faults beneath Pleistocene Lake Lahontan lacustrine fill are expressed as co-located peaks in GPS second invariant (Band 4) and positive areal dilatation (Band 8) under low-relief basin cover (Band 19 muted), where surface scarps are erased but GPS strain sees aseismic creep; catalogue-blind so holdout truth is never used as input.
mechanism: Robust-normalized z(B4) × ReLU(z(B8+)) × sigmoid(-(B19-median)/scale) masked to footprint & >2px off existing_faults.tif, clipped [0,1], score-sorted Poisson-disc thinning at 2.8 px to 37,654 binary dots via vendor/gems57/grid.write_submission mode='zeros' (EPSG:32611, 3730×3292, float32). No catalogue-derived feature; all three bands are GPS/DEM, so zero leakage from withheld fault geometry.
named_non_fault_process: Central Nevada agricultural groundwater withdrawal subsidence bowls, playa evaporite contraction, and irrigation-related anthropogenic strain produce similar second-invariant highs without faulting; mitigated by basin-weight sigmoid and requiring positive dilatation, but residual confound remains — must be tested with InSAR OPERA control (not available in sandbox allowlist).

holdout_dti.design: 4-fold quadrant draw, seed 20, hide_frac 0.20, domain erode 12 px, pooled DTI alpha 0.2 beta 0.8 300 m triangular kernel, measured on raw binary dots (no HGB training) — simple baseline to compare vs H33 raw dots on identical withheld geometry
